How do you want to build your archive?

A personal data server (PDS) hosts an AT Protocol account and its records. Start with a release entry you can edit and export: credit the makers, link to the work, and name the contact for bookings or permissions.

Learn with Mayhem
Follow the virtual hackathon proposal. Bring a question or test a handoff. Participation is free and you can learn without an account.
Publish it yourself
Use a hosted PDS or follow the open self-hosting kit. You can keep your identity if you later migrate.
Commission a template
Proposed service: hire Loptr Lab to build a reusable archive layout for your work and teach you to publish the next entry.
Commission a server
Proposed service: agree on an installation price and handoff. You control the domain, hosting and credentials. An optional maintenance agreement can cover updates, monitoring, backups and restore tests.

One account. A different home.

@made-sick.org is our account. On October 7, 2026, its public identity record changed to point to Eurosky as its account server. Its underlying identity stayed did:plc:o6kuv3yieti2vqrb7ckmd5vg. Followers do not need to follow a new account when the same identity moves.

See the public identity record . The dated identity history records the host change. The server address is https://eurosky.social. The October 7 review did not verify account sign-in or participant publishing; the public identity record alone does not establish those functions.

Handle
The readable name people use to find you: @made-sick.org.
DID
The stable identifier that lets services recognize the same account after a move.
Personal Data Server (PDS)
The service that hosts your account, public repository and uploaded media. You can migrate to another PDS with the same DID.
AppView
A service that gathers public records so an app can show feeds or search. It is separate from your account server.

A server move does not make public posts private or keep every copy in the EU. Each app has its own permissions and policies. Read those before authorizing access; keep private health records, credentials and confidential files out of public records.

Publish with a purpose. Give people a next step.

Use the apps for different jobs: keep one maintained article, start a focused public conversation, and help readers find a useful action. A shared account can connect services, but each app chooses what it indexes and displays. Posting through another client does not automatically reach a new audience.

Publish and discover
Use your existing pckt publication for the article. Check its public records and reader discovery. Try Leaflet Reader before creating another publication. Explore publishing and reader implementations.
Discuss and listen
On mu.social, join a relevant conversation with a sourced question and the article link. Look for existing music-business feeds and follow their inclusion rules; do not mass-tag people or imply their support.
Convene a session
Use Streamplace for an agreed public discussion. Confirm guests, recording permission and moderation first; follow with an accessible transcript and sources.
Learn what helped
Record relevant replies, corrections and professional participation. Use Search Console reporting to assess search discovery separately. These observations do not prove every referral or guarantee reach.

Example: artist rights and royalty transparency

50 Ways to Leave Another supplies the creative and educational context. Made-Sick’s existing cards hold professional, royalty and civic-resource routes. This guide explains how to connect that work to readers; it does not duplicate the directory.

  1. Link to one sourced article and distinguish recording, publishing and distribution agreements.
  2. Start with one question: what information should a royalty statement explain about deductions and recoupment?
  3. Follow with one practical resource, then invite a musician, royalty specialist or lawyer to identify missing evidence and existing protections.
  4. Update the article with attributed responses and corrections. For public-policy questions, use the same questions across offices and distinguish no response from opposition.

Keep private agreements and financial records out of public replies. Do not present an allegation as an established finding or a resource listing as endorsement. This is an example workflow, not a scheduled campaign or a claim that anyone has agreed to participate.
